title: Mathematics: Philosophy

sourceText.admission:
Admission Requirements

The Department of Mathematics has two admission pathways: Early Entrance and Standard Entry. For either pathway, visit the Department website for instructions to declare the major.

• Early Entrance: 

• Minimum course requirements: MATH 200 (or MATH 300), MATH 208

• Grade requirements: Minimum 3.8 grade for each course required for admission

• Standard Entry: 

• Minimum course requirements: MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 126, MATH 200 (or MATH 300), MATH 208

• Grade requirements: Minimum 2.0 grade for each course required for admission; minimum 3.20 cumulative GPA in courses required for admission

The Department of Mathematics does not accept post-baccalaureate applicants.

sections.credentialOverview:
Credential Overview

The Philosophy option allows students to combine mathematics and philosophy. The math courses introduce students to mathematical reasoning; the philosophy courses complement this method of reasoning with methods that have arisen within the historical tradition of philosophy. Students are encouraged to take coursework specifically in the areas of the philosophy of science or mathematics.
sections.credentialCompletionRequirements:
Completion Requirements

68-76 credits

• Core (32-40 credits) 

• Complete one of the following: 

• MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 126, MATH 207, MATH 208

• MATH 134, MATH 135, MATH 136*

• MATH 200, MATH 300, MATH 327, MATH 424

• Advanced Math (16 credits): Four additional mathematics courses at the 300- or 400-level, including at least one two-quarter sequence at the 400-level other than MATH 407, MATH 408, or MATH 409.

• Philosophy (20 credits): PHIL 120 or an upper-level course in logic; PHIL 100, PHIL 160, or PHIL 240; one philosophy course at the 300-level; one philosophy course at the 400-level

• Minimum 2.0 grade in all courses presented to satisfy mathematics major requirements. Minimum 2.00 cumulative GPA in all mathematics courses at the University, including course repeats.

• Minimum 18 credits of graded mathematics courses numbered 300 or higher taken in residence through the UW.

*May receive advanced placement (AP) credit for MATH 124 (after completing MATH 134) and MATH 125 (after completing MATH 135).
